posts.name: Under3
posts.cooked:
Once a gaming group hits a certain size I think you just have to accept you’re often going to need to split the group as very few games support larger groups or if they do aren’t usually optimal at the maximum amount due to things like excessive down time.
Luckily Sentinels is perfect for being able to split if both groups want to play it as there’s more than enough heroes/villains/environments to share. Sure, I get everyone would rather play together if they can, but in my experience it isn’t always practical unfortunately.
From what I can remember off the top of my head 6 seems to be around the sort of amount where a number of games struggle to support gameplay for.

posts.name: NAL0781
posts.cooked:
We play a lot of games with 6, but there is downtime.  Each has their own cup of tea.  Compared to the old Avalon Hill games that we would play though, today's games seem downright optimal.

 

Oddly enough, when we have 3 players, we usually prefer to still play with six heroes (the adverse of the norm).  As I mentioned, the game doesn't feel broken (whereas 2 heroes or 7+ does) & it gives us a chance to try some heroes that we don't typically play.

 

I think the coolest part is the fact that this discussion exists speaks to the strength and appeal of the game that you have people who enjoy it based on a wide variety of number of players.

posts.name: shadowagent
posts.cooked:
ok... lets assume the breaking into 2 groups isn't an option or desirable.

In the past I was a paid game reviewer (and reviews editor) for the gamingreport.com (before being disbanded by F&W), Scry, Game Trade and others under the pen name “Marc Shayed”. I have also have consulted with several game companies on game design... as thus I have a pretty epic game room with 100s of games on my shelves. I have a 100+ year old restored oak library table (3’ x 8’) to game on and wing back chairs. My players/gamers come to my game nights to interact and be social to play games with their friends, spouses and significant others because I can accommodate a large group and we can all get in on the same games. I would like to be able to have SotM to remain our go-to game, however with 6 players the game tends not to be enjoyable.

We have played Advanced rules... still 6 players makes it too easy

We have tried putting a +1 to all "H"s on top of the advanced rules... villains tend to crush the heroes

We have tried 2 villains... 1 starting the round (before player 1), and 1 villain half way through the round (between players 3 &4)... had mixed results...it’s either a slaughter (villains wrecking the heroes in just a few rounds) or it’s a hard fought slug-fest that still ends up with the villains winning.

We have tried 2 teams taking on 2 villains in 2 environments... where if the heroes beat 1 villain, they can leave that site and join in the other's battle... where BOTH villains have an H of 6...  (this was ok... but you have to keep the turns synced and that just makes the game timing a pain)

What I think would be great is a sheet of villain specific rules for 6 players ... ie... (not actual suggestions)
Gloomweaver : at the end of turn, Gloomweaver pulls 1 zombie out of the trash and puts it back into play
Baron Blade : At the start of the turn Baron Blade flips 2 cards from the villain deck and starts with 2 minions in play
The Dreamer : Whenever a Projection is destroyed, the Dreamer deals each Hero 2 psychic damage

so on and so forth... 

I don't think a 1 rule fits all approach will work... but a downloadable and updateable sheet with a rule for each villain may work well. Thoughts?

posts.name: BlueHairedMeerkat
posts.cooked:
As a fan project, I approve whole-heartedly. As an official release... Mnggheeh...

 

If you do want fan-made 'Advanced+' rules, here are some thoughts:

Omnitron - Some kind of defensive boost. Certainly up the component damage threshold, maybe give him some kind of Shielding Wind-y protection and/or stick DR on Adaptive Plating Subroutine?

Cosmitron - Front side, +1DR. Back side, 'at the end of the villain turn, play the top card of the villain deck.'

Dawn - I'm not convinced Dawn can be fixed for six. Getting seven Citizens out on her flip side is just too much...

The Ennead - Start on the flipped side, with all nine Ennies on the table.

Apostate - At the end of the villain turn, shuffle the villain trash and reveal cards until a Relic is revealed. Put it into play.
